title: Magnetic Effects of Electric Current
seo_title: Magnetic Effects of Electric Current Class 10 Science Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Chapter 12)
standard_code: Class 10, Chapter 12: Magnetic Effects of Electric Current
standard_text: Magnetic effects of current: magnetic field, field lines, field due to a current carrying conductor, field due to current carrying coil or solenoid; force on current carrying conductor, Fleming's left hand rule, direct current, alternating current: frequency of AC, advantage of AC over DC, domestic electric circuits.
meta_desc: Free CBSE Class 10 Science worksheets for NCERT Chapter 12: magnetic field lines, the right-hand thumb rule, solenoids and electromagnets, Fleming's left-hand rule, fuses and domestic electric circuits. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: A current makes a magnetic field around it.
key_sub: Fleming's left hand: Field, Current, thrust (Motion).
body_html:
How to think about it

A current-carrying wire has a magnetic field of concentric circles around it; the right-hand thumb rule gives its direction. A solenoid behaves like a bar magnet, and with a soft iron core it makes an electromagnet.

A current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field feels a force, largest when the current is at right angles to the field. Fleming's left-hand rule: forefinger along the field, middle finger along the current, thumb gives the force. Homes in India get 220 V AC at 50 Hz with live, neutral and earth wires, protected by fuses or MCBs.

Example

Current east, field north. Force?

forefinger north, middle finger east

Answer: upwards

Example

A 2,000 W, 220 V geyser. Fuse?

I = 2,000/220 ≈ 9.1 A

Answer: 10 A

Common mistakes

  • Using the right hand for the force on a conductor.
  • Choosing a fuse far bigger than the current needed.
  • Mixing up the colours of live, neutral and earth wires.

faq.q: Why does a fuse protect a circuit?
faq.a: Its thin wire melts when the current is too large, breaking the circuit before wires overheat.

faq.q: What is the difference between AC and DC?
faq.a: DC flows in one direction; AC reverses direction periodically (50 times a second in India, so 50 Hz).

items.q: What is the magnetic field outside a long solenoid like?
c: like the field of a bar magnet
items.e: One end acts as a north pole and the other as a south pole.

items.q: How does the field around a straight wire change as you move away from it?
items.e: Field strength falls with distance.

items.q: When is the force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field the largest?
c: when the current is parallel to the field
when the current is at right angles to the field
items.e: There is no force when they are parallel.

items.q: Why do two magnetic field lines never cross?
c: they always cross at the poles
there would be two directions of the field at one point, which is impossible
items.e: The field has one direction at each point.

items.q: What is the frequency of AC supply in India?
items.e: AC changes direction 100 times a second.

items.q: What colour is the live wire in Indian domestic wiring?
items.e: Neutral is black (or blue) and earth is green.

items.q: Which device is used in homes in place of a fuse in many new buildings?
items.e: It switches off automatically on overload.

items.q: Which sources give direct current (DC)?
items.e: DC flows in one direction only.

items.q: What does the right-hand thumb rule give?
c: the direction of the magnetic field around a current-carrying wire
the direction of the force on a wire
items.e: Thumb along the current; fingers curl in the field direction.

items.q: Who discovered that a current-carrying wire deflects a compass needle?
items.e: This showed that electricity and magnetism are linked.

items.q: What does a compass needle show near a magnet?
c: the direction of the magnetic field at that point
items.e: Its north end points along the field.

items.q: How can you make a solenoid's magnetic field stronger?
c: use more turns, a larger current or a soft iron core
items.e: This is how strong electromagnets are made.

items.q: Why is a separate circuit used for high-power appliances such as geysers?
c: it has a higher current rating (15 A)
items.e: Lights and fans use a 5 A circuit.

items.q: Where is the magnetic field of a bar magnet strongest?
c: near the poles, where field lines are closest
items.e: Crowded lines mean a stronger field.

items.q: Why is the metal body of an appliance earthed?
c: so that any leaked current flows to the earth and does not shock the user
items.e: The earth wire has low resistance.

items.q: What is the potential difference between the live and neutral wires in Indian homes?
items.e: The supply is alternating current at 50 Hz.

items.q: What is the shape of the field lines around a straight current-carrying wire?
c: straight lines parallel to the wire
items.e: Use the right-hand thumb rule for the direction.

items.q: What is the direction of magnetic field lines inside a bar magnet?
c: from the south pole to the north pole
items.e: Field lines are closed loops.

items.q: What happens if the direction of the current in a conductor in a magnetic field is reversed?
items.e: Reversing the field also reverses the force.

items.q: What is the field like inside a long solenoid?
c: uniform, with parallel straight field lines
items.e: It is used to make electromagnets.

items.q: A wire in a magnetic field pointing south feels a force east. By Fleming's left-hand rule, which way does the current flow?
items.e: Forefinger: field (south); thumb: force (east); middle finger: current, towards the top.

items.q: A current flows towards the east in a wire that feels a force downwards. By Fleming's left-hand rule, which way does the magnetic field point?
items.e: Middle finger: current (east); thumb: force (downwards); forefinger: field (south).
